title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck sets up 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes', i.e. building conformal surfaces by cutting and gluing along boundary arcs. The next page applies this to Teichmüller groupoids with boundary and to stable curves. This page continues part B of a local model for gluing a disc to itself.

Setting, from the previous page. Points 1, ζ, ζ̄ lie on the unit circle S¹. β is the arc from 1 to ζ and β̄ the arc from 1 to ζ̄. α is the complementary arc from ζ to ζ̄. φ: β → β̄ is a homeomorphism with φ(1)=1 and φ(ζ)=ζ̄.

Claim B, finished on this page. φ is 'rectifiable' (Grothendieck's term, apparently meaning that φ can be realised as a gluing map). Equivalently there is a continuous f = f_φ: D → D such that:
1) f is holomorphic and injective on the open disc D°; write U = f(D°).
2) f(0)=0 and f(ζ)=f(ζ̄)=1, and f maps α∖{ζ,ζ̄} homeomorphically onto ∂D∖{1}.
3) f|β and f|β̄ are bijections onto a common image I. By 2), I meets ∂D only at 1, so I∖{1} lies in D°.
4) If f₁: β → I and f₂: β̄ → I are the induced bijections, then φ = f₂⁻¹∘f₁.

So f folds the disc: it glues β to β̄ via φ and opens the result as the slit domain U = D∖I. The fold point 1 goes to the tip of the slit inside the disc, and ζ, ζ̄ go to the boundary end 1 of the slit. f is unique. Grothendieck notes the proof uses the uniformization theorem with boundary in ℂ.

Scholie: there are 1–1 correspondences between:
(a) gluable ('rectifiable') homeomorphisms φ: [0,1] → [0,1] fixing 0 and 1;
(b) gluable topological arcs I in D from an interior point to 1, with I ∩ ∂D = {1};
(c) continuous maps f: D → D with properties 1)–3).
The next page adds (d): power series of radius of convergence ≥ 1 that extend continuously to D with these properties.

In modern terms this is conformal welding for slits. A slit disc D∖I is uniformized by the disc. The boundary correspondence on the two sides of the slit is a welding homeomorphism. Conversely, a homeomorphism is a welding iff the slit exists, and the slit is unique when it is removable (e.g. a quasiarc). The role of the construction is a local gluing model ('bouchage'/folding) used to build surfaces in the Teichmüller groupoid with boundary on the next page.
errors: Possible normalization inconsistency. Condition 2) says f(0)=0, and 0 lies in U = f(D°), so 0 cannot lie on the slit I. Yet the figure and Scholie (b), and the earlier normalization 'amenant a en 0, b en 1', describe a slit running from 0 to 1. Either the tip f(1) should be sent to 0, or I in the Scholie should join f(1) (not 0) to 1. The Scholie's 'reliant 0,1' may actually read 'reliant a,1'.

Gap: uniqueness ('f est unique') needs the welding to be unique. That holds only for suitably 'nice' (e.g. conformally removable) arcs, which is presumably encoded in the undefined word 'rectifiable'. As stated it is not justified, since there are non-unique weldings for non-removable curves.

Gap: 'rectifiable' is not defined on this page. It does not mean finite length; it seems to be an ad hoc name for 'is a welding'. If so, the Scholie is a tautological reorganisation, except for the existence claim, which needs a real criterion (e.g. quasisymmetry via the Beurling–Ahlfors / Pfluger theorem).

ideas.what: Folding a disc along two adjacent boundary arcs via a homeomorphism φ, realised by a slit map f: D → D∖I, with φ recovered as f₂⁻¹f₁
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pfluger (1960); Lehto–Virtanen; later Marshall–Rohde (zipper algorithm, Loewner slit maps), Sheffield (quantum zipper)
ideas.where_published: Only hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme (surgery / Teichmüller tower); not developed there

ideas.what: Scholie: correspondence between gluing homeomorphisms of [0,1], slits in the disc ending on the boundary, normalized slit maps, and power series on the disc
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical geometric function theory (Loewner 1923; welding theory 1960s)

ideas.what: Using such local gluings to define Teichmüller groupoids of complex-analytic surfaces with boundary and to plug boundary holes, yielding stable curves (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Sewing / surgery of Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (CFT, 1987), Vafa, Huang (sewing), Kontsevich–Penner style constructions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the Teichmüller tower and surgery informally

missed.claim: Around 1983–84 Grothendieck was building conformal surgery of surfaces with boundary on conformal welding of boundary arcs, as the basic gluing for Teichmüller groupoids with boundary. This parallels Segal's later (1987) sewing formalism for conformal field theory, and modern welding/zipper work on gluing random surfaces, but from an algebraic/Teichmüller-tower viewpoint.
missed.quote: Il y a corr. 1-1 entre les données suivantes: a) Les homéomorphismes rectifiables φ:[0,1]→[0,1] ... b) Les segments topologiques rectifiables ... c) Les applications continues f:D→D
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that the analytic (welding) side of the Teichmüller tower in the Esquisse was being worked out concretely. The welding mathematics itself is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard conformal welding for slit domains, stated with a minor normalization slip. Its interest is only as documentation of Grothendieck's analytic groundwork for surgery and Teichmüller groupoids.
transcription_corrections: In Scholie (b), the phrase transcribed 'I reliant 0,1' may read 'I reliant a,1' in the image. This would be consistent with f(0)=0 and with a slit tip that is not at 0.
The struck-out heading in 3) is illegible; the surviving text reads 'f|β et f|β̄ sont bijectives sur une image, I, ... d'après 2) et I∖{1} est contenu dans D°'.
In 4), 'alors' is an insertion above the line, before φ = f₂⁻¹f₁.
